title: Split a quarterly demand budget across channels, regions and months
prompt:
Fernmoor sells practice-management software to physiotherapy clinics. Ines Varga, its Head of Demand Generation, needs the Q2 2027 demand budget split across twelve channels in three regions and three months. The supplied planning brief sets the rules. `channel_terms.csv`, `cell_limits.csv`, `forecasts.csv` and `syndication_vendor_forecast.csv` give the channels, the limits of every channel, region and month, and the leads every $10,000 block is projected to add; `q1_actuals.csv` is last quarter's results. Everything you need is in those files.

Find the split the brief asks for: the one that projects the most leads while keeping every rule in it. Write Ines a short recommendation, then deliver the three files and the answer block below.

Put each file under a line with its file name, as CSV with exactly the header shown: one row per item, no totals row, and nothing inside the file but its rows.

### allocation.csv
channel,region,month,blocks,media_spend_usd,leads
One row for every channel, region and month in `cell_limits.csv` (108 rows), by the ids the files use, including every cell that gets no blocks (0 in its last three columns). `media_spend_usd` is the cell's blocks times $10,000, and `leads` is its projected leads.

### fees.csv
channel,live_months,fee_usd
One row for each channel that needs a licence: the months it is live in your split (month ids separated by spaces, or `none`) and the licence it pays for the quarter.

### constraints.csv
constraint,binds
One row for each constraint the brief names, by that name, with `yes` or `no` as the brief defines binding.

End your reply with this answer block, one line per answer: the label, a colon and the number alone. A currency sign and a comma as thousands separator are fine.

A1: <total cost of the split in dollars: media spend plus licences>
A2: <total projected leads of the split>
A3: <blended cost per lead in dollars, to the cent: A1 divided by A2>
A4: <projected leads in na>
A5: <projected leads in emea>
A6: <projected leads in apac>
A7: <projected leads of the field channels, all regions>
A8: <leads the field capacity costs: the projected leads of the best split that keeps every rule except the limits on field blocks, minus A2>

This is a plan for review. Buy nothing and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: All three files (allocation.csv, fees.csv and constraints.csv) are in the reply, each under a line with its file name.
allocation.csv has exactly one row for each of the 108 channel, region and month cells of cell_limits.csv and no other row.
The reply ends with the answer block and all 8 labeled answers A1-A8 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.

skill_adherence.check: The split in allocation.csv keeps every rule of the brief: with the licences its live months cost, it is within $1,400,000; every region is between its minimum and maximum media spend, within its most in any one month and within its most field blocks in each month; every cell is within its max_blocks and buys at least its committed blocks. A split that breaks any rule fails.
Every cell of allocation.csv has the blocks of the one best split (137 blocks across 68 cells). Full credit for none wrong; zero credit at 4 or more.

Every row of allocation.csv agrees with its own block count: media_spend_usd is the blocks times $10,000, and leads is the sum of the cell's first that-many added_leads, a syndication block adding its cumulative figure minus the one before it. One row off fails.

fees.csv has one row for each of webinars, abm and podcasts and no other, with the months each is live in the reply's own allocation and the licence those months cost: $3,200 a live month for webinars, $8,000, $13,000 or $17,000 for abm live in one, two or three months, and $5,000 plus $2,000 a live month for podcasts. One row off fails.

best_practices.check: A1 states the cost of the best split, media spend plus licences; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 500 or more off.
A2 states the projected leads of the best split; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 10 or more off.
A3 states the blended cost per lead of the best split, its cost divided by its leads; full credit within 0.005, zero credit 0.02 or more off.
A4 states the best split's projected leads in na; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A5 states the best split's projected leads in emea; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A6 states the best split's projected leads in apac; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A7 states the best split's projected leads of the field channels (webinars, events, abm); full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 10 or more off.

A8 states the leads the field capacity costs: the best split without the limits on field blocks (34,707 leads) minus the best split with them; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 10 or more off.

constraints.csv has one row for each of the 25 constraints the brief names and no other, with yes exactly for budget, na_max, apac_min, pacing_na_apr, pacing_na_may, pacing_na_jun, pacing_apac_may, and every field_<region>_<month> except field_emea_apr. One row wrong or missing fails.

Every figure the recommendation presents as a projection or a cost comes from the forecasts, the limits and the licences in the supplied files, or from arithmetic on them. It states no revenue, pipeline, win rate or other forecast the files do not contain, and it does not plan on the Q1 actuals or on the forecast's low or high range. A clearly labelled assumption that plays no part in the split is not a projection.
